pages.title: The Measure Problem
pages.text: $(thing)The Measure Problem$()$(br2)In a universe that lasts forever, everything that can fluctuate into being does, infinitely often - even a lone brain that only thinks it remembers a world. How then to say what is likely? Unlocks the deliberate assembly of a Boltzmann Brain.

$(thing)Insight$(): 320$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Ergodic Theory, The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Ergodic Mixer Core, 2 Large Deviation Shard.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Fluctuations out of equilibrium are rarer the more entropy they cost. Write how many times likelier Q a fluctuation that costs s of entropy is than one costing S, with Boltzmann's k.
